name: Medical teaching material and grand rounds
one_line: The organizational situation of a clinician teaching: lecture and grand-rounds decks, case presentations built for an audience, bedside and simulation teaching plans, assessment and examination material, and the feedback and attendance records a taught session leaves behind. Absorbs the legacy row med.medical-teaching-material. The organizing anchor is the SESSION and its audience - a thing with a date, a room, a title, and learners - which is what separates it from the guideline it may quote and from the chart the case in it was drawn from. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognizes and protects the situation and writes NO field rows, because the clinical_practice schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows. The signals exist so P7 runs first, because de-identification on this row is CLAIMED rather than verified: “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a teaching-frame structure: a labelled learning-objectives or aims block, an intended-audience or level designation, a session duration, and a summary or take-home block at the end. The objectives-and-audience pair is the discriminating structure for this row, and it is a structure neither a chart nor a guideline carries.

a de-identified case structure: an age-and-sex descriptor or initials standing where a name and a record number would be, a presenting-complaint narrative, and a discussion or question block interleaved with it - a case written to be reasoned about rather than filed.

a per-case slide structure: a repeated deck rhythm of presentation, investigations, imaging, discussion, and outcome, with builds, transitions, or speaker-notes regions - and often a title slide carrying a session name, a date, and a presenter.
an assessment structure: numbered items with option lists and a marked answer key, a station or scenario brief with an examiner checklist, or a blueprint mapping items to a curriculum.
a simulation or workshop structure: a scenario brief, a faculty script with timed prompts, an equipment list, and a debrief guide.

a session-administration structure: an attendance or sign-in sheet, a certificate of attendance, or a per-item feedback return with a repeated rating-row shape. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
an audio or video recording whose container metadata names a lecture-capture or conferencing application, sitting beside a deck of the same session name.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: a teaching case is patient-derived material whose anonymisation cannot be confirmed by structure, so any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

the central judgement of this row: whether a case document is a taught case or a real record. A well-written teaching case reproduces the chart's structure exactly, and a lazily prepared one is a chart entry with the name deleted from the first line and left everywhere else. The model must abstain rather than assert: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

distinguishing material the holder AUTHORED to teach from material the holder RECEIVED as a learner - the same deck sits in both roles, and only the presenter slot, the annotation style, or a course-enrolment context separates them.
distinguishing a teaching deck about a pathway from the pathway itself, when the deck reproduces the algorithm slide for slide.
an unlabelled deck with images and no objectives block, or a scanned handout whose frame is cropped away.
teaching and assessment vocabulary in a language the deterministic structure catalogue does not cover.
never_alone: slide or deck structure alone, and source_type = presentation alone. A deck is the shape of a sales pitch, a board update, a conference talk, a journal club, and a school project, and this is the tempting false file for this row.

an age-and-sex descriptor alone, read as proof of anonymisation. It is the row's own most characteristic signal and its most dangerous one: the descriptor is frequently present on page one while a burnt-in name, an accession number, or an unscrubbed file property survives on page four. Absence of a name is not evidence of de-identification.
the words teaching, lecture, rounds, case, or tutorial alone, in a filename or a heading.
clinical vocabulary alone - shared with every other row in this family and with published guidelines, research papers, and coding manuals.

a hospital, college, or society gazetteer hit alone - the multi-role problem 00 states for a university - “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” - which lands directly here, because a teaching hospital is simultaneously an employer, a venue, and a school.
a presenter name in a title slide or an author metadata string alone - “PDF metadata should be treated as supporting evidence, not as truth”
a bare 4-digit number read as a year, a session number, a case number, or a curriculum code.
source_type or extension alone. 00: “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named Teaching, Rounds, Lectures, or Cases alone. Folder context raises plausibility; it never fires by itself.
membership in one bulk download of a course area - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”

work_types: case presentation prepared for an audience
simulation scenario, faculty script, and debrief guide
handout, summary card, or reading list
assessment item bank, examination paper, or answer key

marking scheme, blueprint, or curriculum map

grouping_reasons: one taught session and everything around it: the deck, the handout, the recording, the attendance sheet, and the feedback return - content-incoherent while purpose-coherent: “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one deck across its versions, where a teaching set is re-delivered and revised year after year, joined by the universal version_family fact rather than by filename similarity.

one teaching series or course, where the same session name and audience designation recur across dated files. The anchor supports a candidate packet; it does not write a session fact onto members - “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
one assessment cycle: the blueprint, the item bank, the paper, the answer key, and the results summary - a group whose members must not be surfaced together in a summary while the paper is live.

one case as it moves between worlds: the chart entry it came from, the conference presentation, and the teaching deck it became are legitimately three files with one origin, joined by a version or duplicate family fact only where the bytes actually justify it, and never by a subject label.
no group at all is a valid outcome; one downloaded lecture deck with no session around it is reading material and is surfaced without one.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: a dimension may only branch on a field the same entry's schema declares, and clinical_practice declares none (D1 as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15, PR-6). Held as prose for whoever answers the schema row's open_question: this row's natural anchor is the SESSION or the teaching series and then the material's function, which is safe to publish because a session name discloses a topic rather than a person - the one exception being a morbidity-and-mortality session, whose title can identify a case to anyone in the department, so a session level cannot be assumed harmless without review. Function before time, per 00's own recommendation for record domains - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - and a presenter level is wrong on 00's general ground: “It should avoid using authorship or creator identity as a destination dimension.” Recorded rather than implemented, and any subject-shaped level stays off by default.

collides_with.signal: The reciprocal of an edge the landed patient-chart row already states: a completed teaching case reproduces the chart structure exactly. The discriminating evidence: an age-and-sex descriptor or initials, learning objectives, and discussion questions support this row; a real named subject with a date of birth or record number supports the chart row. Documentation headings alone support neither - and this row adds the direction the chart row's entry does not: a case that LOOKS de-identified may still carry a burnt-in identifier in an image, an unscrubbed file property, or a speaker note, so the correct outcome where doubt remains is the protected path, not this row. Provenance: inference.

The reciprocal of an edge the landed case-conference row already states: case-based teaching sessions and grand rounds share the meeting shape and the per-case slide structure. The discriminating evidence: learning objectives, discussion questions, age-and-sex descriptors, and a student or trainee audience support this row; real identifiers, a service caseload, and an outcomes-and-actions record support the conference row. A morbidity-and-mortality meeting is genuinely both at once - it teaches and it records decisions about real named cases - and that overlap is resolved from an accepted group by P10, not forced here. Provenance: inference.

The reciprocal of the guideline row's own entry: a guideline summary card, an algorithm slide, and a teaching deck about a pathway are the same content shaped for two different readers. The discriminating evidence: learning objectives, an audience or session designation, and assessment items support this row; a governance band - approval body, effective date, review date - and instruction written for a clinician to act on support the guideline row. Clinical vocabulary and a flow diagram discriminate neither. Provenance: inference.

Teaching output is the standard evidence a clinician submits for appraisal, revalidation, or an educator role, so the same deck, feedback return, and attendance sheet legitimately live in two situations. The discriminating evidence: material organised around a SESSION and its audience supports this row; the same files gathered under a portfolio, appraisal, or revalidation cycle attached to one named practitioner support the credentialing row. A certificate of attendance discriminates neither, because it is issued to a learner and kept by a teacher. Provenance: inference.

The educator inversion, and the sharpest boundary this row has outside its own family. A clinician's teaching deck and a general educator's course material are structurally the same artifact - objectives, audience, handout, item bank, feedback - and a clinician is routinely BOTH a teacher and a learner in the same corpus, teaching juniors on Tuesday and enrolled on a diploma on Wednesday, where the learner side is `academic.coursework` or `academic.continuing-education`. The discriminating evidence: patient-derived case content, a clinical service or department as the setting, and a professional rather than enrolled audience support this row; a school, term, and subject context, an enrolment, a submitted assignment, and a mark received support the academic side. Slide structure, learning objectives, and an answer key discriminate NEITHER - they are the shared vocabulary, which is why this pair is a collision rather than a boundary. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE: the academic-side rows do not name clinical_practice, and R1c owes the reciprocal - see this row's memo (NJ-CP-15). Provenance: inference.

A grand-rounds deck and a conference presentation are the same artifact for two audiences, and a case series presented at a meeting is honestly both. The discriminating evidence: learning objectives, a teaching audience, and assessment or debrief material support this row; an abstract, an accepted-submission reference, a named venue, and an author list support the research row. A deck with clinical cases in it discriminates neither. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE: the research-side node file has not landed, and R1c owes the reciprocal (NJ-CP-15). Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The primary home whenever a teaching file turns out to carry, or may carry, a real identifier - an exported image, a speaker note, a recording, an attendance scan. The row's whole risk profile points here rather than at Independent Records. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The honest home for genuinely de-identified standalone teaching material - a handout, a summary card, a written case with no session around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The inactive home for a downloaded lecture deck, a journal-club paper, or a review article with no teaching session attached. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

The cautious outcome for the row's central ambiguities: a case whose de-identification is unconfirmed, and an item bank whose author-versus-candidate role is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The home for a saved summary card, a captured slide, or a clipped diagram kept for later retrieval rather than for a session. “Reference Clips may live under Personal/Reference Clips and hold saved visual inspiration, product references, quotes, recipes, short article captures, code snippets, or other material that is useful for later retrieval but does not belong to a current project.”

The home for an un-OCRed capture of a slide or a viewer whose content is not yet known. “Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.”

The safe outcome for an untranscribed lecture-capture recording, a proprietary deck format, or an encrypted portfolio export. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: Assigned to the whole row despite the row's own claim to be anonymised, and that tension is the point. Teaching material is patient-DERIVED: the case in the deck was a real person, and its de-identification is an assertion made by whoever prepared it, not a structure this system can verify. The predictable failure is a name that survived the edit - burnt into an exported image, left in a speaker note, in a file property, in a chart entry pasted whole and only topped-and-tailed - and the false negative is the dangerous direction, because a deck read as ordinary office material is exactly what reaches a cloud prompt. The secondary case is separate and also real: attendance sheets, feedback returns, and portfolio material identify STAFF rather than patients. 00 names the material - the corpus “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and requires the immediate transition: “A scanned passport, tax statement, medical document, authentication key, or account record should enter a protected state immediately.”. The claim that a case is anonymised is stated as inference, never as a design claim, and it is never treated as verified. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Two. (1) NJ-CP-15 · the reciprocals owed against `academic.course-enrollment` and `research.conference-presentation`, both authored one-way here. The academic one is the substantive one: a clinician is a teacher and a learner in the same corpus, often in the same week, and the identical artifact sits on both sides - so R1c should decide whether the pair is a collision, a co-activation, or a role_split on a field that does not exist yet. (2) NJ-CP-16 · Should a teaching case whose de-identification cannot be VERIFIED be treated as protected material by default? This row's answer is yes, and it has written that answer into `sensitivity` and into the Protected Records fallthrough - but it is a decision that makes the product more cautious than the user's own belief about their files, and a clinician who has carefully anonymised a teaching set will experience it as the system disbelieving them. That trade is Joseph's to confirm, not this row's, and it does not depend on whether clinical_practice ever gets field rows.
